doc.title: Annie Ross interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Singing with Lionel Hampton and views on big-band singing
summary: She recalls the Hampton trumpet section with Art Farmer, Clifford Brown and Quincy Jones, and says she prefers small groups to big bands.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Yeah. That was around the early 50s with Hampton?
Yeah, ’51 I think, if my notes are correct at all. And a vocalist in front of a big band, is it taxing?

I don’t like it. I feel too restricted. I’d much rather sing with a quartet, maybe piano, bass, drums and guitar or I love flutes and saxophones. There are some people who are brilliant at it. I don’t feel I’m one of those. Joe Williams was — I mean Sarah — any singer. But I felt looser when I was with a smaller group.
